prompt.context_jp: S&Fの業績は今後数年の見通しさえ立たないほど低迷していた。
prompt.prompt_jp: S&Fの業績___今後数年の見通しさえ立たないほど低迷していた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that establishes S&F's performance as the topic of the sentence.

feedback.correct_en: は marks 業績 as the established topic — the narrator is commenting on the known subject (S&F's performance) rather than introducing it as new info.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would signal new information or exhaustive identification, which doesn't fit this scene-setting line. を is a direct-object marker and ungrammatical here.

contrast_examples.en: (As for) the performance, it was sluggish. [topic]
The performance (specifically) was sluggish. [newly introduced fact]

prompt.context_jp: カウンターの隅には、あの見覚えのある徳利が、まるで主を待つように置かれていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: カウンターの隅には、あの見覚えのある徳利___、まるで主を待つように置かれていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that introduces the sake bottle as a newly-noticed sight.

feedback.correct_en: が introduces the sake bottle as new, discovered information — Satonaka notices it on the counter. The scene foregrounds its existence.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would imply the bottle was already an established topic, but it's being introduced here. に is a location/direction marker and doesn't fit.

contrast_examples.en: A sake bottle was (there) placed. [new discovery]
The sake bottle, it was placed (as for it)… [presupposes known]

prompt.context_jp: やがて口を開いたとき、その声はいくぶん硬かった。
prompt.prompt_jp: やがて口を開いたとき、その声___いくぶん硬かった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking 'his voice' as the topic being described.

feedback.correct_en: は treats その声 as the topic — the narrative continues describing something already contextually given (Satonaka's voice when he finally spoke).
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark new/exhaustive info, but the voice is tied to the preceding clause's subject. で doesn't fit grammatically.

contrast_examples.en: (As for) his voice, it was stiff.
It was his voice (specifically) that was stiff.

prompt.context_jp: 「俺 Ｓ＆Ｆ 辞めるよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 俺、Ｓ＆Ｆ___辞めるよ。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking S&F as the thing being quit.

feedback.correct_en: 辞める takes を to mark the organization one leaves. Here S&F is the direct object of quitting.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would treat S&F as subject, which is wrong. に would mean 'to S&F' as a destination.

prompt.context_jp: 理想を掲げながらも自分ひとりでは実現しきれず苦しんできた後輩の目は、しかし驚くほど澄んでいた。
prompt.prompt_jp: …苦しんできた後輩の目___、しかし驚くほど澄んでいた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle fitting the contrastive 'however' that follows.

feedback.correct_en: は sets up the contrast marked by しかし — despite struggling, his eyes (topic, in contrast) were clear. Contrastive-は fits perfectly.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce the eyes as new, missing the deliberate contrast. も (also) doesn't match the contrastive logic.

prompt.context_jp: 「私は あんなに強くなれない だから 正社員の採用試験 片っ端から受けようと思う」
prompt.prompt_jp: 私___ あんなに強くなれない。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that contrasts 'me' with Omae (who IS that strong).

feedback.correct_en: Contrastive-は: Aki contrasts herself with Omae — 'I (unlike her) can't be that strong.' This is textbook contrastive は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would exhaustively identify her as the one who can't be strong, which misses the implicit comparison. も would mean 'me too', opposite of her meaning.

prompt.context_jp: 「僕が守ります」
prompt.prompt_jp: 僕___守ります。
prompt.prompt_en: Mita declares himself as the one who will protect her — choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: が here is exhaustive/identificational: 'It's I (and no one else) who will protect you.' This is a classic volunteering / self-identification pattern.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make 'me' the topic and weaken the declaration. を would mark 僕 as an object, which is wrong.

contrast_examples.en: I'll (be the one to) do it.
As for me, I'll do it (others may not).

prompt.context_jp: 「賢ちゃんには 人を動かす力が あったってことだな」
prompt.prompt_jp: 賢ちゃんには 人を動かす力___ あったってことだな。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking 'the power to move people' in this existence construction.

feedback.correct_en: ある/いる existence constructions use が to mark what exists. Here it's revealing that Ken had this ability — new, foregrounded information.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make the ability the topic, but here it's being newly identified/asserted. を doesn't go with ある.

contrast_examples.en: He does have power (contrastively, but lacks something else).

prompt.context_jp: 宮部が去り、社内には久しく忘れていた明るい空気が流れていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 社内には久しく忘れていた明るい空気___流れていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that introduces this bright atmosphere as something newly present.

feedback.correct_en: が introduces the bright atmosphere as a newly noticeable phenomenon — a presentational description of the changed office.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would presuppose the atmosphere as already-known topic. に doesn't fit as the subject marker for 流れる.

contrast_examples.en: The atmosphere (we know of) was flowing.

prompt.context_jp: 「俺はね 終身雇用が好きなんだよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 俺___ね 終身雇用が好きなんだよ。
prompt.prompt_en: Shoji is stating his own preference — contrasting with Satonaka's path. Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: は marks 俺 as the topic and implicitly contrasts Shoji's view with Satonaka's independence. Standard 〜は〜が好きだ pattern.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would be an exhaustive 'it's me who likes…' — grammatically odd before another が-phrase and semantically wrong here. を is impossible with 好き.

contrast_examples.jp: 俺は終身雇用が好きだ。
contrast_examples.en: As for me, I like lifetime employment.

contrast_examples.jp: 俺が終身雇用が好きだ。

prompt.context_jp: 「自分が導入したＡＩに クビ切られるとはな」
prompt.prompt_jp: 自分が導入したＡＩ___ クビ切られるとはな。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking the AI as the agent of a passive 'got fired by'.

feedback.correct_en: In passive constructions, に marks the agent performing the action. Miyabe was fired BY the AI he himself introduced.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark the AI as subject of an active sentence. で means 'by means of' and sounds instrumental, weakening the ironic agent reading.

contrast_examples.en: He was fired by the AI.

prompt.context_jp: 浅野は苦笑いを浮かべ、湯呑みのお茶を一口すすった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 湯呑みのお茶___一口すすった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking the tea being sipped.

feedback.correct_en: すする takes a direct object with を — the tea is what gets sipped.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make the tea the subject. に would give a destination/target reading, incorrect for consuming.

prompt.context_jp: 窓の外には春の光が差し込み、真新しい看板を柔らかく照らしていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 窓の外には春の光___差し込み…
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle introducing the spring light as a newly-observed scene detail.

feedback.correct_en: が introduces 春の光 as new presentational detail — the narrator paints a vivid scene with freshly-noticed elements.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would presuppose the light as topic. を would be ungrammatical as 差し込む here is intransitive.

prompt.context_jp: 見紛うはずのない、あの人だった。派手な着物、大きく結い上げた髪、そして手にしたマイク。
prompt.prompt_jp: 店の奥から現れたその姿___、一同は言葉を失った。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking 'at that figure' — they lost their words AT the sight.

feedback.correct_en: The actual sentence uses に to mark the stimulus they reacted to — 'at that figure, everyone lost their words.' に marks the trigger of the reaction.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make the figure the subject of 失った, which is wrong (一同 is the subject). は would set it as topic but mismatches the causal 'at the sight' reading.

contrast_examples.jp: その姿に言葉を失った。

prompt.context_jp: S&Fの綱領には社員も派遣も一丸となってとうたわれているが、現場の実感はまるで違う。
prompt.prompt_jp: …とうたわれているが、現場の実感___まるで違う。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking the on-the-ground reality in contrast to the stated ideal.

feedback.correct_en: Contrastive-は: the charter says one thing, but (in contrast) the reality on the ground is completely different. The が clause before sets up the pivot.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce the reality as new neutral info, losing the deliberate contrast with the charter. も (also) contradicts the 'different' meaning.

contrast_examples.jp: 理想は高いが、現実は厳しい。
contrast_examples.en: The ideals are high, but reality is harsh. [contrast]

prompt.context_jp: 雑談は自然と、去った男の話へと流れていった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 雑談___自然と、去った男の話へと流れていった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking 'the chatter' as the topic.

feedback.correct_en: は takes 雑談 as topic — the narrator describes what happened to the ongoing conversation. Classic topic-comment structure.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce the chatter as new/exhaustive, but it's already part of the scene. に doesn't fit as subject marker.

contrast_examples.en: (As for) the chatter, it flowed on.

prompt.context_jp: 「初めての派遣切りで さすがに ___ましたから」
prompt.prompt_jp: 初めての派遣切りで、さすがに ___ましたから。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb meaning 'was feeling discouraged/bummed'.

feedback.correct_en: めげる means to be discouraged or dispirited — fits Omae being bummed after her first termination.
feedback.incorrect_en: もめる means to quarrel/have trouble, not emotional defeat. つげる means 'to inform' and doesn't match.

contrast_examples.en: I don't get discouraged even if I fail.

prompt.context_jp: 棚に並ぶ空きボトルの数を思えば、塵も積もれば___となるとはよく言ったもので…
prompt.prompt_jp: 塵も積もれば___となる
prompt.prompt_en: Complete the proverb 'Even dust piled up becomes ___.'

feedback.correct_en: 塵も積もれば山となる ('even dust piles up into a mountain') — small amounts accumulate. Fits perfectly with Omae's growing bar tab.
feedback.incorrect_en: 川 (river) and 海 (sea) don't appear in this fixed idiom. The proverb specifically uses 山.

contrast_examples.jp: 塵も積もれば山となる。
contrast_examples.en: Even dust piled up becomes a mountain.

prompt.context_jp: 「後悔しても構いません しなかった後悔は 日に日に ___なりますから」
prompt.prompt_jp: しなかった後悔は 日に日に ___なりますから。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word that means 'bigger/greater' here.

feedback.correct_en: The adverbial form 大きく attaches to なる ('to become big'). 日に日に大きくなる = 'gets bigger day by day.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 大きい is the plain adjective form and doesn't combine with なる directly. 大きさ is a noun ('size') and breaks the pattern.

prompt.context_jp: 「もう___になったの？」
prompt.prompt_jp: もう___になったの？
prompt.prompt_en: Aki teases Mita for enjoying overwork. Choose the slang for 'corporate slave.'

feedback.correct_en: 社畜 (lit. 'company livestock') is slang for someone who sacrifices everything for their company — fits the teasing tone.
feedback.incorrect_en: 社長 (CEO) and 社員 (employee) don't carry the sarcastic bite Aki is going for.

contrast_examples.en: I don't want to become a corporate slave.
I want to become a full-time employee.

prompt.context_jp: 宮部蓮三は、コスト削減という名の人員濫伐によって、この会社の血肉を___きた男である。
prompt.prompt_jp: この会社の血肉を___きた男である。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb meaning 'has been scraping away/draining.'

feedback.correct_en: 削り取る ('shave/scrape off') captures the sense of gradually stripping away the company's substance through layoffs.
feedback.incorrect_en: 受け取る is 'to receive,' which contradicts the meaning. 切り取る ('cut off') is close but less idiomatic for this gradual, violent stripping of 'flesh and blood.'

prompt.context_jp: 東海林はふと窓の外に目をやり、___な笑みを浮かべた。
prompt.prompt_jp: ___な笑みを浮かべた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word meaning a 'wry/ironic' smile.

feedback.correct_en: 皮肉な笑み is an 'ironic/wry smile' — fits Shoji's amused-but-rueful reaction about Miyabe being fired by his own AI.
feedback.incorrect_en: 豪華 (gorgeous) and 素直 (honest/straightforward) don't match the ironic tone of this moment.

prompt.context_jp: 「あいつ ___で認めやがった」
prompt.prompt_jp: あいつ ___で認めやがった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the phrase meaning 'by reflex / conditioned reflex.'

feedback.correct_en: 条件反射 ('conditioned reflex') nails the joke — Omae auto-confirmed her real name without thinking.
feedback.incorrect_en: 無条件降伏 means 'unconditional surrender' — related word but different meaning. 絶対安静 means 'absolute bed rest.'

contrast_examples.jp: 条件反射で手が動いた。

prompt.context_jp: 「そのうち ___きますよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: そのうち ___きますよ。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb meaning 'she'll come swooping/flying back.'

feedback.correct_en: 舞い戻る evokes a dramatic, almost theatrical return — perfect for the legendary Omae, who always reappears.
feedback.incorrect_en: 立ち止まる means 'to stop walking.' 引き下がる means 'to withdraw/back down,' the opposite of coming back.

prompt.context_jp: The master of the restaurant offers Satonaka a seat and invites him to share Omae's bottle.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds more natural as a casual, friendly invitation from the shopkeeper?

choices.text: よかったら 一緒に飲みませんか？
よかったら 一緒に飲むのはいかがでございますか？

feedback.correct_en: 〜ませんか is the natural polite-but-warm invitation form in an izakaya setting. It's friendly without being stiff.
feedback.incorrect_en: 〜のはいかがでございますか is overly formal keigo, suited to department store clerks, not a small restaurant owner chatting over sake.

contrast_examples.jp: ご一緒にお飲みになりませんか。
contrast_examples.en: Would you care to drink together? [very formal]

prompt.context_jp: Satonaka is inviting his senior Shoji to start a company together, over sake.
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds more natural for this heartfelt, casual invitation between close colleagues?

choices.text: 東海林さん 一緒にやろうよ
東海林さん 一緒にやりましょうではありませんか

feedback.correct_en: やろうよ with the volitional + よ is natural for an earnest, intimate proposal between close associates over drinks.
feedback.incorrect_en: やりましょうではありませんか is stilted, speechy, and far too formal for a quiet, personal moment at an izakaya.

contrast_examples.en: Shall we do it together? [polite neutral]

prompt.context_jp: Omae is leaving the office and declaring her next move to the executives.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line better fits Omae's cool, defiant-yet-polite farewell?

choices.text: 自分のやり方で あなた方に勝とうと思っています
自分のやり方で あなたたちをやっつけるつもりだぞ

feedback.correct_en: The 〜と思っています framing paired with あなた方 is poised and polite yet carries defiance — signature Omae.
feedback.incorrect_en: やっつける…ぞ is blunt, masculine street talk that clashes with Omae's icy professionalism.

contrast_examples.jp: 勝とうと思っています。

prompt.context_jp: Greeting a colleague returning from consecutive business trips at the office.
prompt.prompt_en: Which greeting is most natural for welcoming back a hard-working colleague?

choices.text: 連日の出張 ご苦労さまです
連日の出張 疲れ果てたでしょう本当に

feedback.correct_en: ご苦労さまです is the standard set phrase acknowledging a colleague's labor — concise and appropriate in this office setting.
feedback.incorrect_en: 疲れ果てたでしょう本当に is awkward and overly dramatic, not a conventional workplace greeting.

contrast_examples.en: Thanks for your hard work. [more neutral, among peers]

prompt.context_jp: Omae defending her late-career debut as a singer.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing captures the natural, slightly proverbial tone of her retort?

choices.text: 夢をかなえるのに 年なんか関係ないよ
夢をかなえる件につきまして年齢は無関係であります

feedback.correct_en: 〜のに〜なんか関係ない is the natural idiomatic way to dismiss a factor — delivered with よ it feels sharp and confident.
feedback.incorrect_en: The B option uses stiff bureaucratic phrasing (〜につきまして、〜であります) that would never come out of Omae's mouth in a casual roast.

contrast_examples.jp: 年齢は無関係であります。
